summary: The Protect Our Letter Carriers Act of 2025 authorizes $1.4 billion annually for five years to the Postal Service for high-security collection boxes and electronic arrow keys, requires the Attorney General to designate a prosecutor in every district to coordinate mail-related crime cases, and directs the Sentencing Commission to treat assaults or robberies of postal employees like those against law enforcement officers.

scores.thoughts: Section 3 authorizes $1.4 billion annually for fiscal years 2026-2030 (totaling $7 billion) to the USPS for security upgrades. This directly expands federal appropriations and government outlays.
The bill contains no provisions related to taxes, tax rates, or revenue measures.
The bill contains no provisions related to healthcare policy, coverage, or markets.
The bill contains no provisions related to firearms regulations or gun rights.
The bill contains no provisions related to immigration, borders, or pathways to citizenship.
The bill contains no provisions related to abortion access or restrictions.
The bill contains no provisions related to military or defense spending.
The bill contains no provisions related to environmental protections or regulations.
The bill contains no provisions related to welfare programs, food assistance, or social safety net programs.
The bill contains no provisions related to schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill contains no provisions related to drug enforcement, decriminalization, or legalization.

Sections 4 and 5 require dedicated federal prosecutors for postal crimes and direct the Sentencing Commission to treat assaults/robberies against postal employees the same as those against law enforcement officers. This strengthens prosecution and increases sentencing severity.
The bill contains no provisions related to trade, tariffs, or globalization.
The bill authorizes new spending without offsets or debt-reduction measures, but does not directly address deficit policy or debt prioritization.
The bill contains no provisions related to LGBTQ+ legal protections.
The bill contains no provisions related to foreign aid.
The bill contains no provisions related to voting access, election integrity, or voter ID.
The bill mentions electronic mailbox keys but does not address data privacy, tech regulation, or surveillance oversight.
The bill addresses safety for postal workers but contains no provisions on union rights, collective bargaining, or employer flexibility.
The bill contains no provisions related to religious exemptions or civil rights enforcement.
